answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when each identity must forge its reputation from verified work: newcomers lock a refundable stake — a sable-dark deposit of real value, not a hollow promise — then complete small verifiable tasks checked by randomly assigned peers, earning signed receipts hash-chained to the previous one. Reputation accrues only from that ledger, so buying a pile of throwaway identities buys nothing: each fake locks its own stake and passes real checks, and one forged receipt breaks the chain and slashes the deposit.
